clue.text: Dull pedantries being re-expressed

indicators.note: something re-expressed is put another way, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's pedantic quibbles are tedious when they are repeated in other words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being re-expressed' tells you to rearrange the letters of PEDANTRIES, which give exactly the ten letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pedestrian is prosaic and lacking imagination, a synonym of dull.

clue.text: Formative toy for Shakespeare?

parts.note: a toy building where children act out make-believe, which is also the name for the kind of theatre where Shakespeare's works were staged

explanation.surface: A question about which childhood plaything shaped the young Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as asking what toy formed the playwright, but the word wanted is both a child's play-hut and an Elizabethan theatre such as the Globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small toy house for children's games and a theatre building, Shakespeare's workplace.

clue.text: Manure's a brown colour? Good

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour, as of a horse

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether manure is a brown colour, and approves.
explanation.definitionFit: Dung is animal excrement spread on fields as fertiliser, the same thing as manure.

clue.text: Dodge succeeded — that is on record

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
id est is the Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A successful evasion is now documented, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' gives the full Latin ID EST rather than the usual IE; 'on' simply places it before the record, EP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to avoid or evade it, as a verb meaning to dodge.

clue.text: Mechanical figure's basis found in book? On the contrary

indicators.note: these words say one piece sits inside another, and the closing phrase swaps which is inside which
this phrase reverses the stated relation, so the book goes inside the basis rather than the other way round

parts.note: the root of something is its basis or origin

explanation.surface: A question about whether a mechanical figure's origin lies in a book, answered by saying the reverse is true.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the basis would go inside the book; 'On the contrary' flips 'found in' so B goes inside ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is an automaton, a machine built to resemble and act like a person.

clue.text: Country taking a line from another country

indicators.note: taking something away from a word removes those letters from it
names the word the letters are removed from

parts.note: Australia is the country being trimmed
A as written, plus L, the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: One nation annexes a border line belonging to its neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and L (a line) from AUSTRALIA and the European country is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation in central Europe, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: One suggesting chap goes round northern area, near port

parts.note: someone who drops hints is a hinter

indicators.note: the chap goes round, or encloses, the letter for northern

parts.note: a lad is a chap or young man

explanation.surface: Someone making hints wanders about a northern region close to a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinterland is the land behind a coast or port, supplying it with trade.

clue.text: Woman gives surprised cry when snatching revolver

indicators.note: the cry snatches, or grabs and holds, the gun inside itself

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of surprise or discovery
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A woman exclaims in surprise as she grabs a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's first name, as of the crime writer Christie.

clue.text: Hard to move in bustling Reading

indicators.note: a bustling place is full of busy movement, so the letters of the town are stirred up

explanation.surface: A busy scene in the Berkshire town of Reading, where something is stuck fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a large town west of London; here its letters are fodder for 'bustling', giving GRAINED after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ingrained is deeply fixed, like dirt worked into fabric, so it is difficult to shift.

clue.text: Superior stud

definitions.meaning: one's superior at work is one's manager or chief
a raised ornamental knob, as on a shield, is called by the same word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a manager over others and also a decorative raised knob or stud.

clue.text: A little petulant, etc, hypersensitive

indicators.note: only a little of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Describing someone as rather peevish and oversensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of 'petulant' and ends inside 'hypersensitive'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means irritable and touchy, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Secret eco-rites involved in recycling

indicators.note: recycling processes material into a new form, so the letters are reprocessed into a new order

explanation.surface: Hidden environmental ceremonies are part of reusing waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' rearranges the eight letters of ECO-RITES; 'involved in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an initiated few, so it is private or arcane.

clue.text: Guess work as a magician will involve misleading etc

indicators.note: the magic word takes in, or contains, the other letters

parts.note: to conjure is to do magic tricks

indicators.note: misleading means leading astray, so the three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guess that a magician's work includes misdirection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misleading' rearranges ETC to ECT, which goes inside CONJURE after its J.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjecture is an opinion formed without proof, a supposition.

clue.text: Communist at university inviting one in to study

indicators.note: the communist invites, or welcomes inside, the letter for one
confirms the letter goes in, completing the container signal

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
A means one, as in a single item
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A communist student invites someone round to do some work.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'at university' is British usage: students go up to university and come down at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To read up on a subject is to research it, a phrasal verb for studying.

clue.text: Idiot agitated bear in agony

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: pain is suffering or agony

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A distressed bear writhing in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns BEAR into EABR, which sits inside PAIN after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-brain is a stupid person, someone with a brain the size of a pea.

clue.text: Bloke, new, trapped in a marsh or stagnant pool

parts.note: Bill is a common man's name, standing for any bloke

indicators.note: the letter for new is caught inside the marsh

parts.note: A as written, plus bog, a marsh

explanation.surface: A man, newly arrived, gets stuck in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: BILLABONG is an Australian word: a backwater cut off from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is an Australian backwater or oxbow lake, often a still pool.

clue.text: McSantos unconvincing as this?!

indicators.note: a name that rings false needs rearranging to give the real thing

explanation.surface: Someone called McSantos fails to pass as a native of a particular country.
explanation.walkthrough: McSantos looks Scottish at the start and Iberian at the end; rearranged, the letters give a man from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The name McSantos has a Gaelic prefix but a Spanish ending, so it is an unconvincing name for a man from north of the border.

clue.text: A fool heading off, about to fail in interview

indicators.note: the shortened fool goes round the word for failing
the heading, or first letter, of the word is cut off

parts.note: a dunce is a slow-witted person
to die is to fail or stop working, as of an engine

explanation.surface: A clown loses his head, close to collapsing during a job interview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' cuts DUNCE to UNCE; 'about' puts it round DIE, giving U-DIE-NCE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a formal meeting with an important person, such as an audience with the Pope.

clue.text: Director is a big noise, suppressing a sense of superiority

indicators.note: the noise holds down, or contains, the letter

parts.note: din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A film director, an important person, keeps his arrogance under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a big noise' reads as an important person; here the noise is DIN, which takes in the second 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is contempt for what one considers beneath one, a haughty attitude.

clue.text: Joyful batsman's beginning to get supple

indicators.note: the start of the word, its first letter, is used

parts.note: lithe means supple and flexible

explanation.surface: A cricketer is delighted to start limbering up.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means happy and carefree, so it is a synonym of joyful.

clue.text: Hear about the ultimate in fashion

indicators.note: the word for hearing a case goes round the other piece

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court
the end is the ultimate point

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen to the latest in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is a judge's job, to try a case, not listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trendy is fashionable and up to date.

clue.text: Argument — especially as it's really 500?

parts.note: a quarrel; read as a sentence, the word claims the Roman numeral for 500 equals one, which is false, so it is apt that the word means falling out

explanation.surface: A dispute over whether a figure is truly five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after its fourth letter: the Roman numeral D (500) 'is unity', which is plainly wrong when D is really 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Disunity is disagreement and lack of harmony, which an argument shows.

clue.text: Bridge player with no hearts? That's about right

indicators.note: says the preceding pieces go round, or about, the next one

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A card player with no cards in one suit thinks that is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass point, so a bridge player can be North.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four seats are named by compass points, and the partner of South sits at the top of the diagram.

clue.text: Father has opening — in this role?

definitions.text: Father has opening — in this role?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a rent is a tear or opening in fabric

explanation.surface: A man has a chance to fill a vacancy, as a father.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a father holds this role.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is a mother or father figure to a child, the role the clue asks about.

clue.text: Note reduced skirt

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note in American usage

explanation.surface: A remark that a skirt has been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the final M of MINIM; the result is also a short skirt, nicely tied to 'reduced'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a very short skirt, short for miniskirt.

clue.text: Just following broadcast

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Something being right after it has gone out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means impartial and equitable, a synonym of just.

clue.text: Purchasing system whereby armour is given to monks?

parts.note: mail is armour made of linked metal rings
an order is a religious community of monks

explanation.surface: Kitting out a monastery with chain armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whereby' and 'is given to' link the pieces: armour given to monks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is buying goods from a catalogue for delivery by post.

clue.text: Bridge opponents making a protest? Charming!

parts.note: East and North are on opposing sides at the bridge table
protesters chant slogans

explanation.surface: Card players staging a demonstration, greeted with sarcasm.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South partner East and West, so E and N are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanting means delightful and captivating, so it is a synonym of charming.
